_units: kJ/mol, per gas-phase atom, at T = 298.15 K
_meaning: Each value is the standard enthalpy of formation of the monatomic gas, dH_f(X,g,298.15K), i.e. the enthalpy required to take one mole of element X from its standard state (H2/N2/O2 ideal gas at 1 bar; graphite for carbon) to gas-phase atoms X(g). The value already includes the ZPE and finite-temperature contributions of the standard state, so no vibrational analysis of H2/N2/O2 (or of graphite phonons) is needed at runtime.
_source: CODATA Key Values for Thermodynamics (Cox, Wagman & Medvedev, Hemisphere Publishing, 1989), as redistributed by the NIST Chemistry WebBook.
_previous_values_note: Earlier H/N/O values (217.354, 471.454, 248.645) were computed from W1-F12 electronic energies + ORCA thermal corrections, and C used a separate constant of 718.1 kJ/mol hard-coded in stages.py. They were all within ~1.5 kJ/mol of CODATA but introduced a dependency on a private high-level calculation; CODATA values are experimentally derived and are the conventional reference for dH_f tables, so we use them directly and unify all four elements in this file.
